request.spec:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each claim now shows its status log, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

Each line reads `<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>`, oldest first. A new claim gets its `DRAFT` line when it's added, and each status change after that adds a line.

- **Stored data:** a new `claim_log` table (migration `V29__claim_log.sql`). It keeps the status, the user, the sheet's today and the due as worked out at that moment (`n/a` when there is no rate).
- **Server:** a new `LogClaimStatus` step runs right after the claim is saved in three places: adding a claim, quick-add, and the status-change actions (open, settle, approve, reject, void). It doesn't write the audit file. A refused change never reaches it, so nothing is logged.
- **How the due is worked out:** I moved the existing settle-time calculation from `ApplyClaimAction` into a shared helper, `ClaimDueNow`, which both settling and the log now use. So a settle line shows the same due that gets fixed, including any late charge. Other lines show the live due at that moment, using the claim's new status.
- **Server response:** claim responses now include a `log` list. The full claims list fetches every log on the sheet in one query.
- **Front end:** a new `ClaimLog` component adds the `claim-log-line` elements to each claim row.

Editing or moving a claim adds no line, since neither changes its status.
